fieldMarks: White coat, long and shaggy in winter, with a crest of erect hair along the spine and rump and long leg hair ('pantaloons').
Both sexes have short, black horns that are never shed and grow annual rings.
Females' horns are more slender and bend back sharply; males' horns are more evenly curved.
Males are markedly larger than females (Alaska: about 280 lb vs 180 lb).
behavior: Nannies form nursery groups with kids and young; billies stay in small bachelor groups except during the late October–early December rut.
Active from sunrise to mid-day and again at dusk; digs shallow beds for resting and dust bathing.
Grazes sedges, forbs and low shrubs in alpine meadows in summer; browses in winter.
Moves from alpine summer range to treeline or old-growth forest in winter.
habitat: Steep, rocky cliffs and bluffs in alpine and subalpine terrain.
range: Native from southeast Alaska through western Canada to Washington, western Montana and central Idaho. Introduced populations exist in South Dakota, Colorado, Washington and on several Alaskan islands.

lookalikes.name: Dall sheep
lookalikes.howToTell: Dall sheep are also white but lack the mountain goat's black horns and prefer drier country.
